- SOC 2 Type II in place (summary attached); we can provide the full report under NDA.

Medivault asks outstanding:

2) Clarify BYOK flow for key rotation and revocation in Private deployment.
3) HIPAA/GDPR coverage for ePHI and cross-border processing.

Raj / team —

Quick tech note from our crypto lead (me) on the revocation/rotation items: 

1) Revocation flow (summary):
- Customer triggers key deletion/revocation in their KMS -> KMS issues event -> Redwood control plane marks key as revoked and updates routing.
- Serving nodes consult the control plane on key status; any new seal/unseal/decrypt requests using the revoked key are rejected.
- KV cache: live KV cache contains encrypted blobs, not plaintext. When a key is revoked we remove the relevant key IDs and mark cache entries as stale. On-the-fly decrypt attempts will fail and the application will receive an error; we also support an explicit cache-invalidation API so you can proactively clear entries cluster-wide.

2) Immediate termination guarantees:
- We guarantee denial of new decrypts within one control-plane propagation window (typ. < 30s in Dedicated/Private). We cannot retroactively decrypt previously served plaintext that has already left the sandbox of the runtime and been persisted elsewhere by customer systems.

3) HSM specifics:
- Supported: AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and vendor HSMs (e.g., Thales Luna) for on-prem/Private. We provide guidance for FIPS 140-2 L2/L3 procurement and integration.

4) Audit/logging:
- Request-level metadata and key usage logs are retained per customer policy; default retention is 90 days with options to extend. We can export logs to your SIEM (S3, Cloud Storage, or push to Splunk/Datadog).

If helpful I can convert this into a short technical appendix (1 page + diagram) for your questionnaire.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Cryptography Engineer – Redwood Inference
